result.title: Poison-then-Hide: Finetuning-Activated Backdoor Attack on Pretrained Vision Encoders
result.summary: Backdoor attacks threaten the integrity of machine learning models by allowing attackers to control model behavior through triggers. Models can be compromised during finetuning by backdoor attacks through either poisoned data or adversarial training objectives. Because existing finetuning-activated attacks assume limited domain shift or frozen encoder layers, they often fail under full-model finetuning. We target a stealthy finetuning-activated attack where a dormant backdoor is implanted in a pretrained encoder, and later activated by finetuning on clean downstream data. We propose Poison-then-Hide, a novel attack that remains effective when the entire model is finetuned in a domain transfer. Our approach consists of three components: trigger optimization, base encoder poisoning, and targeted unlearning to conceal the backdoor. We evaluate our method on six datasets and three model architectures, and achieve state-of-the-art (up to 97%) attack success rates. We find that jointly learning the benign target task alongside the poisoning is critical to the attack's success. We demonstrate standard detection and mitigation defenses cannot fully remove the backdoor, which can reappear after benign finetuning.

AI.brief_summary: 提出「Poison-then-Hide」攻击：在预训练视觉编码器中植入休眠后门，经干净下游数据全模型微调后激活，通过触发优化、编码器投毒与定向遗忘隐藏后门，在六个数据集上取得最高 97% 的攻击成功率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「休眠于编码器状态、微调后才显现」的机制可反向用作探针，核查视觉编码器中的细节信息在训练与微调后是否仍被保留、何时真正参与输出，或可供设计 LVR 中视觉内容保留与因果作用的诊断。
